chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-02.title: Simplify
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-02.body:
$\csc x=\frac1{\sin x}$ and $\cot x=\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}$, so the integrand equals $1$.

**Answer: $x+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-03.title: Chain rule
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-03.body:
$\frac d{dx}\cos(\cos(\cos x))=-\sin(\cos\cos x)\cdot\bigl(-\sin(\cos x)\bigr)\cdot\bigl(-\sin x\bigr)=-\sin(\cos\cos x)\sin(\cos x)\sin x$, so the antiderivative is $-\cos(\cos(\cos x))$.

**Answer: $-\cos(\cos(\cos x))+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-05.title: Substitute $u=\sec x$
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-05.body:
Write the integrand as $(\sec x)^{-1/2}\cdot\sec x\tan x$. With $u=\sec x$, $du=\sec x\tan x\,dx$: $\int u^{-1/2}du=2\sqrt u$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{\sec x}+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-07.title: Simplify
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-07.body:
$e^{\ln x}=x$ and $\ln e^x=x$, so the integrand is $2x$ and $\int_1^{10}2x\,dx=100-1=99$.

**Answer: 99**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-08.title: Odd function
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-08.body:
The integrand is odd and the interval is symmetric about $0$, so the integral is $0$.

**Answer: 0**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-13.title: Floor function
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-13.body:
The integrand is $\lfloor1/x\rfloor$. On $\left(\frac13,\frac12\right)$ it equals $2$ (length $\frac16$), on $\left(\frac12,1\right)$ it equals $1$ (length $\frac12$), and on $(1,3)$ it is $0$. So the integral is $\frac26+\frac12=\frac56$.

**Answer: $\frac56$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-14.title: Odd function
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-14.body:
The integrand is odd and absolutely integrable (it decays like $e^{-x^2}$), so the integral is $0$.

**Answer: 0**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-15.title: Split at integers
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-15.body:
On $(k-1,k)$ we have $\lceil x\rceil=k$ and $\lfloor x\rfloor=k-1$, so the integrand is $kx^k-(k-1)$.
- $k=1$: $\int_0^1x\,dx=\frac12$.
- $k=2$: $\int_1^2(2x^2-1)dx=\frac{14}3-1=\frac{11}3$.
- $k=3$: $\int_2^3(3x^3-2)dx=\frac{3\cdot65}4-2=\frac{187}4$.

Sum: $\frac12+\frac{11}3+\frac{187}4=\frac{611}{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac{611}{12}$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-17.title: Split where $\sin x=\cos x$
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-17.body:
$\sin x\ge\cos x$ exactly on $\left[\frac\pi4,\frac{5\pi}4\right]$. There $\int\sin x\,dx=\cos\frac\pi4-\cos\frac{5\pi}4=\sqrt2$. On the rest, $\int_0^{\pi/4}\cos x\,dx+\int_{5\pi/4}^{2\pi}\cos x\,dx=\frac{\sqrt2}2+\frac{\sqrt2}2=\sqrt2$. Total $2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt2$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-18.title: Rewrite as $\cot^2x$
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-18.body:
$\cos x\csc x\cot x=\frac{\cos^2x}{\sin^2x}=\cot^2x=\csc^2x-1$, so the antiderivative is $-\cot x-x$.

**Answer: $-x-\cot x+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-19.title: Recognise a derivative
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-19.body:
Let $g=-\frac1{1-x^2}$. Then $g'=-\frac{2x}{(1-x^2)^2}$, so the integrand is $\frac12g'e^g$, with antiderivative $\frac12e^g$.

**Answer: $\frac12e^{-1/(1-x^2)}+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-21.title: Split the numerator
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-21.body:
$x^2+\cos^2x=(1+x^2)\cos^2x+x^2\sin^2x$, so the integrand equals $\cot^2x+\frac{x^2}{1+x^2}=\csc^2x-\frac1{1+x^2}$. Hence the antiderivative is $-\cot x-\arctan x$.

**Answer: $-\arctan x-\cot x+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-22.title: Factor
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-22.body:
$\sqrt{e^{3x}+e^x}=e^x\sqrt{e^x+e^{-x}}$ and $e^{2x}-1=e^x(e^x-e^{-x})$, so the integrand is $\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}{\sqrt{e^x+e^{-x}}}$, which is the derivative of $2\sqrt{e^x+e^{-x}}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{e^x+e^{-x}}+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-23.title: Differentiate the answer (or parts twice)
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-23.body:
Let $F=-\frac{\cos(\ln x)+2\sin(\ln x)}{5x^2}$. Then $F'=\frac{2(\cos+2\sin)}{5x^3}-\frac{-\sin+2\cos}{5x^3}=\frac{\,2\cos+4\sin+\sin-2\cos\,}{5x^3}=\frac{\sin(\ln x)}{x^3}$. (Equivalently, substitute $x=e^t$ and integrate $e^{-2t}\sin t$ by parts twice.)

**Answer: $-\frac{\cos(\ln x)+2\sin(\ln x)}{5x^2}+C$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-27.title: Union of two half-discs
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-27.body:
The two functions are the upper unit half-circles centered at $(1,0)$ and $(2,0)$ (each defined where the root is real: $[0,2]$ and $[1,3]$). The integral is the area of the union of the two half-discs: $\frac\pi2+\frac\pi2-(\text{overlap})$.

The two unit circles have centers at distance $1$, so the overlap of the full discs is a lens of area $2\cdot\frac\pi3-\frac{\sqrt3}2$ (formula $2r^2\cos^{-1}\frac d{2r}-\frac d2\sqrt{4r^2-d^2}$). The lens is symmetric about the $x$-axis, so the overlap of the upper half-discs is $\frac\pi3-\frac{\sqrt3}4$. Hence
$$\text{union}=\frac\pi2+\frac\pi2-\left(\frac\pi3-\frac{\sqrt3}4\right)=\frac{2\pi}3+\frac{\sqrt3}4\approx2.5274.$$
Check by direct integration: the curves cross at $x=\frac32$ and the integral equals $2\int_0^{3/2}\sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}dx=2\left(\frac\pi4+\frac\pi{12}+\frac{\sqrt3}8\right)$, the same value (also confirmed numerically).

**Answer: $\frac{2\pi}3+\frac{\sqrt3}4$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-29.title: Dyadic intervals
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-29.body:
On $[2^{-k},2^{-k+1})$ ($k\ge1$) the integrand is $2^{-k}$ and the length is $2^{-k}$, so the integral is $\sum_{k\ge1}4^{-k}=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-30.title: Partial fractions
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-30.body:
Since $x^3+1=(x+1)(x^2-x+1)$ and $x^2-2x=(x^2-x+1)-(x+1)$, we get
$$\frac{x^2-2x}{x^3+1}=\frac1{x+1}-\frac1{x^2-x+1}.$$
Then $\int_0^1\frac{dx}{x+1}=\ln2$ and $\int_0^1\frac{dx}{(x-\frac12)^2+\frac34}=\frac2{\sqrt3}\Big[\arctan\frac{2x-1}{\sqrt3}\Big]_0^1=\frac2{\sqrt3}\cdot\frac\pi3=\frac{2\pi\sqrt3}9$.

**Answer: $\ln2-\frac{2\pi\sqrt3}9$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-31.title: Split the fraction
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-31.body:
The numerator is $(\tan x+\sec^2x)+(\sec^2x+2\sec^2x\tan x)$, and $\sec^2x+2\sec^2x\tan x=\frac d{dx}(\tan x+\sec^2x)$. So the integral is $\int_0^{\pi/4}1\,dx+\Big[\ln(\tan x+\sec^2x)\Big]_0^{\pi/4}=\frac\pi4+\ln3-\ln1$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi4+\ln3$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-33.title: Jumps of the floor function
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-33.body:
The integrator $\lfloor x\rfloor$ jumps by $1$ at $x=1,2,3$ and is constant elsewhere, so $\int_0^3(x^2+1)\,d\lfloor x\rfloor=(1+1)+(4+1)+(9+1)=17$.

**Answer: 17**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-34.title: Rationalise
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-34.body:
$\frac{1-\sin x}{1+\sin x}=\frac{2}{1+\sin x}-1$ and $\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{1+\sin x}=\Big[\tan x-\sec x\Big]_0^\pi$ (continuous extension) $=2$. So the integral is $4-\pi$.

**Answer: $4-\pi$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-36.title: Partial fractions
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-36.body:
Factor $x^5+3x^2+x=x(x^4+3x+1)$. With $g=x^4+3x+1$ we have $9x+4=4g-x\,g'$ (since $4g-xg'=4x^4+12x+4-4x^4-3x=9x+4$), so
$$\frac{9x+4}{x\,g}=\frac4x-\frac{g'}g.$$
Therefore $\int_1^2=\Big[4\ln x-\ln g\Big]_1^2=4\ln2-\ln\frac{23}5=\ln\frac{80}{23}$.

**Answer: $\ln\frac{80}{23}$**

chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-38.title: Partial fractions
chmmc-cmm-2023-integration-final-38.body:
$(x^2+1)(x^2+4)=x^4+5x^2+4$ and $(x^2+2)(x^2+3)=x^4+5x^2+6$, so the integrand is $1-\frac2{(x^2+2)(x^2+3)}=1-2\left(\frac1{x^2+2}-\frac1{x^2+3}\right)$. Integrating, $\int\frac{dx}{x^2+a^2}=\frac1a\arctan\frac xa$ gives $x-\frac2{\sqrt2}\arctan\frac x{\sqrt2}+\frac2{\sqrt3}\arctan\frac x{\sqrt3}$.

**Answer: $x-\sqrt2\arctan\frac x{\sqrt2}+\frac2{\sqrt3}\arctan\frac x{\sqrt3}+C$**
